info.title: OPDC API
info.description: A subset of the Twinn REST API (version 3): the routes this example calls. The full reference is at https://twinn.engineering/developers.

post.description: Record an allocation, moving stock and writing job cost per status and purpose.

200.description:
A successful write.

`200`, not `201`, and the name says succeeded rather than created because
three of the four things `201 Created` asserts are not true here:

- **There is no `Location` to send.** `201` SHOULD carry one, and v3 has no
GET-by-id route to point it at. The read surface is
`POST /{entity}/query`. A `201` that can never populate `Location` offers
a caller nothing a `200` does not.
- **Not every write creates.** `/purchase-order-receipts` updates an existing
purchase order. Receiving against a purchase order is a mutation, and `201`
would be flatly wrong on it.
- **An idempotent replay is not a creation.** `Idempotency-Status: replayed`
below says so in the same response. With `201` as the happy path, one
logical operation would report two different success codes depending on
whether it was a retry, which is precisely the distinction a caller should
not have to branch on.

What comes back is a result document (record numbers, the resolved period,
the GL and job-cost postings), not a pointer to a newly addressable resource.
That is `200`-shaped.

202.description:
The write outlived the wait and is still running or queued. **This is not success**: nothing may
have been written yet. `Location` names the request; poll it for the outcome.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before polling.

400.description: Bad request. Includes unknown or misspelled fields, which v3 rejects rather than dropping.

401.description: Authentication failed or the key is not authorised for this operation.

403.description:
The company is set up read-only (`COMPANY_READ_ONLY`): Twinn reads its data and
never changes it, so this write was refused and nothing was executed. It is not
retryable. Making the company writable is done where the Twinn agent is set up,
by whoever administers the company's database.

404.description:
The entity, document or record does not exist.

On a read this is the **unknown-entity** case: `POST /api/v3/prats/query` is a
404 whose `detail` names `prats`, rather than the framework's own 404 with no
body or an empty 200. 79 entity names is a lot of surface to typo, and a
mistyped entity that answers `{"data": []}` looks exactly like an empty result.

409.description:
The request conflicts with state the server already holds.

Two unrelated conditions share this status, and the `type`/`X-Error-Code`
distinguishes them:

- `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`: the same `Idempotency-Key` was already used for a
  **different** request (a different body, or the same body on a different
  route). The `detail` says *"this key was used for a different request; use a
  new key"*, because the commonest way to arrive here is a request that was
  dispatched, failed downstream (a `422`, say), was corrected, and retried under
  the same key. The corrected body **is** a different request, so the fix is a
  new key.
- `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT`: a request with this key is still running. Carries
  `Retry-After`, and it is short: the holder either answers or its 90-second
  lease elapses.
- `DUPLICATE_TRANSACTION`: a transaction number already posted as a ledger
  transaction, with different lines. Nothing to do with the header; decided on the customer's own SQL Server,
  not here.
- `LOCK_CONFLICT`: an unlock attempt against a lock another user holds. Listed
  because it shares the status, **not** because a document write returns it: it
  is raised only by the maintenance un-lock utility.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Set on `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT`.

413.description:
The request, or its answer, is larger than this API key allows
(`MESSAGE_TOO_LARGE`). Nothing was sent, run or written. The body names the
limit, the size and the direction: narrow the request (or page a read with a
smaller page), or ask your Twinn administrator to raise the key's limit. Not
retryable as it stands, and it does not use up an `Idempotency-Key`: the
corrected request may be sent under the same key.

422.description:
The request is well-formed but cannot be applied: a closed posting period, an
out-of-range coded value, unbalanced debits and credits, or amounts that do
not agree with their lines.

**On a read there is exactly one condition and it is `SAGE_SCHEMA_MISMATCH`:** a
column or table the projection expects and this Sage build does not have. Sage
schemas drift between installations, so a field this specification declares can
be absent from a particular customer's database.

423.description:
The company is not taking requests right now (`COMPANY_LOCKED`), and nothing
was executed. `reason` says why: the company is locked for Sage maintenance,
or someone is using it exclusively in Sage (for example, balances are being
recalculated). `Retry-After` states the back-off, rather than leaving it to
prose.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying.

429.description: Rate limited (`RATE_LIMITED`): this API key sent more requests than its rate limit allows. `Retry-After` says when to retry.

500.description: An unexpected server-side failure. The message is redacted; quote `correlationId`.

502.description:
Sage itself refused the operation: `SAGE_ERROR`, the taxonomy's catch-all for a
database-side failure such as a constraint, a deadlock, a permission or a dropped
connection.

**Retryable, and deliberately with no `Retry-After`.** The code is retryable but
carries no number, because there is no honest one to give: a deadlock clears in
milliseconds and a revoked permission never clears. The two statuses this
contract does publish a back-off for (`423`, `504`) are the two where the server
knows what it is waiting for.

**This is not a 500.** The API is a gateway and the failure is the upstream's,
which is what `502` says and what lets you distinguish "Sage said no" from "the
gateway broke" without reading prose. `SAGE_SCHEMA_MISMATCH` is split out of it
at `422` for the one database-side failure your *request* can be wrong about;
every other database-side failure lands here.

503.description:
The API key is provisioned but switched off by Twinn, with the
operator's reason in the body. `SERVICE_DISABLED`, `503`, retryable, and it
carries the taxonomy's `Retry-After: 300`.

**Decided before the handler and before the route matters**, so it is reachable
on every v3 route (reads and writes alike) and carries no
`Idempotency-Status`: nothing was reserved, nothing was dispatched, and your
`Idempotency-Key` is not burned. Distinct from `423`, which is the
operator-held *maintenance* lock on an otherwise enabled key and which the body
attributes to a holder.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. `300`, from the taxonomy.

504.description:
The request was accepted but the on-premises Sage service did not answer in
time. **The outcome is unknown.** Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`; do not
retry without one.

403.description:
The request names a field this API key may not read. `FORBIDDEN`, 403.

Some fields hold sensitive, personal or pay data and are returned only to a key
with the matching permission. Without it they are left out of every row, and naming
one in `select`, `filters`, `orderBy` or `matchFields` is refused rather than
answered, so a filter cannot reveal a value. `errors[].field` says where each
such field was named. Remove it, or ask your Twinn administrator for the
permission.

get.description:
The request's outcome, or `202` while it has none.

**Once the outcome is known this answers exactly what the original call would have answered**:
the same status, `X-Error-Code` and body, so one parser serves both. The response is held for 24
hours after the outcome; after that, and for a request that was answered at once, the answer is
`200` with a `RequestStatus` summary. `OPDC-Request-State` on every answer says which.

`wait` holds the call until the outcome arrives or the wait passes, whichever is first.
Disconnecting from a poll cancels nothing.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: How long to hold the call for an outcome: seconds, or a duration such as `25s`; at most 30.

(`MESSAGE_TOO_LARGE`). Nothing was sent, run or written. The body names the
limit, the size and the direction: narrow the request (or page a read with a
smaller page), or ask your Twinn administrator to raise the key's limit. Not
retryable as it stands, and it does not use up an `Idempotency-Key`: the
corrected request may be sent under the same key.

422.description:
The request is well-formed but cannot be applied: a closed posting period, an
out-of-range coded value, unbalanced debits and credits, or amounts that do
not agree with their lines.

**On a read there is exactly one condition and it is `SAGE_SCHEMA_MISMATCH`:** a
column or table the projection expects and this Sage build does not have. Sage
schemas drift between installations, so a field this specification declares can
be absent from a particular customer's database.

423.description:
The company is not taking requests right now (`COMPANY_LOCKED`), and nothing
was executed. `reason` says why: the company is locked for Sage maintenance,
or someone is using it exclusively in Sage (for example, balances are being
recalculated). `Retry-After` states the back-off, rather than leaving it to
prose.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying.

429.description: Rate limited (`RATE_LIMITED`): this API key sent more requests than its rate limit allows. `Retry-After` says when to retry.

500.description: An unexpected server-side failure. The message is redacted; quote `correlationId`.

501.description:
The server does not implement this for this entity. Distinct from 404: the
route exists and the entity exists, but the specific thing asked for does not
apply to it.

On a read route, its one instance is a change-stamp filter
(`lastUpdated`, `createdSince`) on an entity with no such column:
`CHANGE_STAMP_UNSUPPORTED`, with the field named in the body. Sage maintains no
general modification timestamp, so this is a permanent property of some
entities rather than a backlog item, and no amount of waiting will make those
entities filterable by change stamp.

One write endpoint returns this status: `POST /ap-payments`, for a payment
method other than `check` or a vendor credit applied, neither of which it
records yet (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED`).

502.description:
Sage itself refused the operation: `SAGE_ERROR`, the taxonomy's catch-all for a
database-side failure such as a constraint, a deadlock, a permission or a dropped
connection.

**Retryable, and deliberately with no `Retry-After`.** The code is retryable but
carries no number, because there is no honest one to give: a deadlock clears in
milliseconds and a revoked permission never clears. The two statuses this
contract does publish a back-off for (`423`, `504`) are the two where the server
knows what it is waiting for.

**This is not a 500.** The API is a gateway and the failure is the upstream's,
which is what `502` says and what lets you distinguish "Sage said no" from "the
gateway broke" without reading prose. `SAGE_SCHEMA_MISMATCH` is split out of it
at `422` for the one database-side failure your *request* can be wrong about;
every other database-side failure lands here.

503.description:
The API key is provisioned but switched off by Twinn, with the
operator's reason in the body. `SERVICE_DISABLED`, `503`, retryable, and it
carries the taxonomy's `Retry-After: 300`.

**Decided before the handler and before the route matters**, so it is reachable
on every v3 route (reads and writes alike) and carries no
`Idempotency-Status`: nothing was reserved, nothing was dispatched, and your
`Idempotency-Key` is not burned. Distinct from `423`, which is the
operator-held *maintenance* lock on an otherwise enabled key and which the body
attributes to a holder.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. `300`, from the taxonomy.

504.description:
The request was accepted but the on-premises Sage service did not answer in
time. **The outcome is unknown.** Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`; do not
retry without one.

post.description:
Query this entity.

POST, not GET, and it stays POST: the filter tree is too large and too nested
for a query string. A read that is a POST is a smaller surprise than a URL
that has to be chunked.

400.description: Bad request. Includes unknown or misspelled fields, which v3 rejects rather than dropping.

401.description: Authentication failed or the key is not authorised for this operation.

403.description:
The request names a field this API key may not read. `FORBIDDEN`, 403.

Some fields hold sensitive, personal or pay data and are returned only to a key
with the matching permission. Without it they are left out of every row, and naming
one in `select`, `filters`, `orderBy` or `matchFields` is refused rather than
answered, so a filter cannot reveal a value. `errors[].field` says where each
such field was named. Remove it, or ask your Twinn administrator for the
permission.

404.description:
The entity, document or record does not exist.

On a read this is the **unknown-entity** case: `POST /api/v3/prats/query` is a
404 whose `detail` names `prats`, rather than the framework's own 404 with no
body or an empty 200. 79 entity names is a lot of surface to typo, and a
mistyped entity that answers `{"data": []}` looks exactly like an empty result.

WriteHeaders.dryRun.name: dryRun
WriteHeaders.dryRun.description:
Run the write and roll it back instead of committing it.

The document is validated, the whole cascade executes against your live Sage
data inside one transaction (the general-ledger journal, the balance
propagation, the job costs, the inventory movement), and then the transaction
is rolled back. You get the same result body a real post would have returned,
including the amounts and the accounts the posting would have touched, so
this answers "what would this do" against real data rather than against a
guess.

**No rows are committed. Two things are still consumed, and this is not a
defect we can fix from here.** Ledger reference numbers come from a SQL Server
sequence and identity columns from the tables themselves, and neither is
transactional: a rolled-back transaction does not give them back. So a dry run
leaves permanent gaps in those sequences, exactly as a genuinely failed post
does. If gapless numbering matters to your auditors, do not dry-run in bulk
against production.

**Every identifier in a dry-run response is provisional and will never
exist.** `recordNumber`, `id`, the ledger transaction's record number: all of
them were real inside the transaction and are gone after it. Do not store
them, and do not use them to correlate a later real post.

`Idempotency-Key` is **ignored** on a dry run rather than rejected, so a
client that always sets one keeps working. Nothing is reserved and nothing is
stored, which means a dry run never burns a key and never replays: post for
real afterwards with whatever key you like.

The response body carries `dryRun: true`, so it is self-describing and a
caller cannot mistake one for a committed write.

WriteHeaders.idempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
WriteHeaders.idempotencyKey.description:
Idempotency key, Stripe-style.

The server stores the key with its response for **24 hours** and replays the
stored response on a repeat. **This is the fix for the retry problem**: `504`
is a documented, retryable outcome, and without a key a caller cannot tell
whether Sage committed.

Scope is `(API key, Idempotency-Key)`: per key, not per customer, so two
integrations at one customer that both mint keys from a natural identifier
cannot collide. The **route and the request body are part of the fingerprint,
not the key**: the same key sent with a different body, or to a different
endpoint, is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` rather than a wrong-shaped replay.
The fingerprint is taken over the decoded request, so re-serialising the same
payload with different whitespace or key order is the same request.

**What is stored is the response that was sent, and it is stored if and only
if the request reached the on-premise service.** So a `422` or a `502` is
stored too, and a caller who corrects the body must use a **new** key. Nothing
decided before dispatch (an unknown field, a validation failure, a missing
script) burns the key, so the corrected retry executes rather than colliding.

Replays are marked `Idempotency-Status: replayed`. A concurrent duplicate is
refused with `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` and a `Retry-After` rather than
being executed twice.

At most 128 characters, printable only. Recommended but not required here, so
that a first integration is not blocked on generating one; a write without a
key is not replay-safe and the contract says so rather than pretending
otherwise. It **is** required on `/purchase-order-receipts`.

WriteHeaders.prefer.name: Prefer
WriteHeaders.prefer.description:
How to wait, as RFC 7240 preferences.

- `wait=<seconds>` shortens how long the call is held for the answer (default 25, at most 30).
- `respond-async` answers `202` with the request id at once, without waiting.

A write that has not finished when the wait ends answers `202 Accepted` with a `Location`
header naming `/api/v3/requests/{id}` rather than failing. **A `202` is not success**: follow `Location` for the
outcome, which is exactly what this call would have answered.

WriteHeaders.startBy.name: OPDC-Start-By
WriteHeaders.startBy.description:
How long, in seconds, the write may wait for the on-premise agent to start it (default 60, at most
900), for example to ride out an agent restart. A write not started by then is never started:
it resolves to `503 REQUEST_EXPIRED` and nothing is written.

WriteHeaders.traceparent.name: traceparent
WriteHeaders.traceparent.description:
W3C trace context. Send it and it is propagated to the on-premise service
and into the server logs for the request.

This is the only correlation header the API accepts: there are no bespoke
context-id or integration-id headers.

AllocationPurpose.description:
Why an allocation exists, and therefore whether it produces a job cost.

The purpose is stated explicitly with this field. `description` is free text
and has no effect on posting.

CompanyLockReason.description: Why the company is not taking requests.

recordNumber.description:
Sage's "Cost Code#", a decimal with three places: the value every `costCode`
foreign key carries.

unitDesc.description:
Sage's "Unit".

Spelled `unitDesc` here, while the other entities carrying a unit of measure
spell it `unitDescription`: one concept, two published names.

division.description:
The cost division this code rolls up to. Query the cost-division lookup
(`CostDivision`).

Note the spelling: this field is `division`, while the same value on
`Subcontract` is published as `divisionNumber`.

inactive.description:
`Y` when the cost code is retired and should not be offered for new work;
empty (or `N`) otherwise.

A one-character flag, not a boolean: Sage stores a character here and this
contract publishes what Sage stores. **Spelled `inactive` here and
`isInactive` on clients, employees, equipment, jobs, parts, paygroups and
vendors.**

CostCode.description:
The cost-code lookup (6-5 Cost Codes).

**This is what every "query the cost-code lookup" pointer in this contract
resolves against**, including `JobCost.costCode`. Cost codes are defined per
company, so they are never enumerated here; this endpoint is how a code becomes
a description.

## `recordNumber` is a decimal

Sage carries a cost code with three decimal places, so `recordNumber` is a
decimal string (`"1.500"`), exactly as every `costCode` foreign key to this
entity is. Filter it with the same string a `costCode` carries.

## Five of Sage's nine fields are not returned

This endpoint returns the code, its description, its unit, its cost division and
the inactive flag. Sage also holds two workers' compensation codes, a wage
maximum, a department and a note on a cost code, and none of those five are
returned.

**Note the spelling of the inactive flag on this entity.** It is published here
as `inactive`, while the same flag is published as `isInactive` on clients,
employees, equipment, jobs, parts, paygroups and vendors. One concept, two
names; filter and select by the name this entity publishes.

recordNumber.description: Sage's "Cost Type#", a single digit, so `1` to `9`, and no more.

costTypeName.description:
The cost type's name.

**Published as `costTypeName` here and as `typeName` on the other type
lookups**: one underlying field under two names.

CostType.description:
The cost-type lookup (6-3 Cost Types).

**This is what every "query the cost-type lookup" pointer in this contract
resolves against**, including `JobCost.costType` and `LedgerAccount.costType`.

`1` Material, `2` Labor, `3` Equipment, `4` Subcontract and `5` Other are Sage
presets; **`6` to `9` are defined per company**, and Sage allows no more than
nine: the record number is a single-digit numeric, which is the schema
enforcing the limit. All four of the user range are in use at some
installations, so `6`-`9` must never be hardcoded. That is why this is a lookup
endpoint and not an enum.

**This API validates `costType` nowhere and defaults it to `1` on three write
paths**, so a cost whose type is unknown is silently classified as Material.

A cost type has only a record number and a name, and both are returned.

Decimal.description:
A decimal quantity or amount.

Encoded as a JSON **string** at its native scale in both directions, never as
a JSON number, because a JavaScript client rounds a value like `36.303` through
a float, and forcing a fixed scale on the way out is a lossy transformation
dressed up as formatting. Values are returned at the scale Sage stores them at
and are never rounded or truncated to two places. An amount of money on a write
result always carries at least two decimal places: `10.50`, never `10.5`.

An amount of money on a write request takes at most two decimal places:
`10.50` and `10.500` are accepted, and `10.505` is refused as
`400 FIELD_INVALID`, naming the field. Prices, costs per unit, rates,
quantities, hours and percents keep their own scale.

ErrorCode.description:
**The error taxonomy. There is exactly one, and this is it.**

The same codes are carried in the `X-Error-Code` response header on both API
versions, so a client that already branches on that header sees no new
vocabulary here.

**Codes are append-only.** A code's spelling and meaning never change once
published, and a failure mode that stops existing keeps its code reserved
rather than having it reused. It is the one part of a failure you may safely
branch on in code rather than by pattern-matching prose.

A code maps to `Problem.type` as `https://twinn.engineering/errors/` plus the
code lowercased with underscores replaced by hyphens: `PERIOD_CLOSED` becomes
`https://twinn.engineering/errors/period-closed`.

or.description: At least one child must match.

FilterNode.description: A recursive boolean expression. Exactly one of `and`, `or` or `match` is set.

recordNumber.description: The Sage record number.

transactionNumber.description:
The caller-supplied ticket number. A string, not an integer, and not
generated; the write endpoint takes it as `ticketNumber`.

jobNumber.description:
The job this allocation is for: the `Job` entity's `recordNumber`, not a job
cost.

Not typed `RecordNumber` (`@minValue(1)`): a `LOCATION_TRANSFER` allocation
has no job and stores `0`. Only a `JOB_REQUISITION` requires one, and only
that purpose produces a job cost (see `AllocationPurpose`).

phaseNumber.description: The job phase: the `JobPhase` entity's `phaseNumber`. `0` when unset.

addressLine1.description:
The first address line. The four address fields and `cityName` / `stateCode` /
`zipCode` are **copied from the job** at insert, not supplied by the caller,
so they are a snapshot of the job's address at the time the allocation was
recorded and will not follow a later edit to the job.

stateCode.description: The state or province code. See `addressLine1`.

status.description:
The allocation's status, and it decides what stock moves rather than merely
describing the row. `1` and `2` move nothing, `3` reduces available quantity,
`4` reduces available and both on-hand figures; inventory history is written
for `3` and `4` only. See `InventoryAllocationStatus`.

costOrder.description:
The allocation's order number, as Sage shows it under "Order #".

On a row this API created it is the write's `orderNumber`, or empty when none
was sent; the ticket number is `transactionNumber`.

transactionDate.description: The allocation date. Date, not an instant.

approvalDate.description: The approval date. Date, not an instant.

deliveryDate.description: The delivery date. Date, not an instant.

invoiceDate.description: The invoice date. Date, not an instant.

deliveryMethod.description: How the goods are delivered. Free text. The write endpoint takes it as `deliveryVia`.

description.description:
Free-text description of the allocation.

**Whether a job cost is written is decided by `purpose`**
(`AllocationPurpose`), which the write result derives and returns — not by
this text. It once was: an exact comparison against
`"To Requisition Stock to Job"` drove the accounting cascade off free text.
On a row written before that change, this field is still the only evidence of
intent.

ledgerRecord.description:
The ledger reference this allocation was stamped with, set to the drawn
sequence number at status `3` and `4`, and to `0` otherwise.

Where it resolves at all it resolves against the `LedgerTransaction` entity's
`ledgerRecord`, **not** its `recordNumber`: a ledger transaction carries both
identifiers, both unique, and on some company databases they agree on every
row while on others they agree on almost none.

**When it is non-zero it points at a ledger transaction that was never
written.** The allocation consumes a number out of the ledger sequence and
stamps it here, on the inventory-history rows and on the job cost without
posting any journal. For a job requisition that is more than cosmetic: a real
cost lands against the job with no GL entry behind it, and the dangling
reference makes job cost and the ledger look reconciled when they are out of
step by construction.

Not typed `RecordNumber` (`@minValue(1)`) because `0` is a normal value here,
matching `PayableInvoice.ledgerRecord`.

period.description:
The period the allocation posted into.

Sage spells this differently on a document than on the rows a posting
produces; both are published as `period`, so the split is invisible to a
caller and matters only to someone writing SQL against the database directly.

enteredDate.description: The date the allocation was entered. One of the values `createdSince` filters on. Date, not an instant.

changedAt.description:
When the record was last changed, in Sage or through this API, in UTC. A
record not changed since it was entered carries its `createdAt`.
`changedSince` filters on it, and it can be sorted on.

createdAt.description: When the record was entered, in UTC.

changedBy.description:
The Sage user who last changed the record, or who entered it if it has not
been changed since: Sage's login name, as Sage stores it.

userName.description: The Sage user who entered it. Defaults to the SQL login when the caller sends none.

noteText.description: Free-text notes on the allocation. Line breaks are `\n`; the important note, the part Sage pops up when the record opens, is in `importantNote`. A filter on `noteText` matches the whole note, the important note included, and refuses a `|`.

importantNote.description:
The note's important part: the text Sage shows in a pop-up ("Important Note!") when the
record is opened. Line breaks are `\n`; empty when the note has none. Read only, and not
usable in a filter, a sort or a match: filter on `noteText`, which matches the whole note.
It is only ever added to (`POST /api/v3/notes`), never replaced or cleared.

InventoryAllocation.description:
An inventory allocation (Sage 12-2), as read.

**What the allocation actually moves is decided by `status`.** See
`InventoryAllocationStatus`, which states what each value actually moves. What
it does **not** do is post a journal: the flow writes no ledger
transaction at all, while still consuming a ledger sequence number and stamping
it on this row. See `ledgerRecord`.

**Only `id` and `recordNumber` are required.** Every other field is optional
because a query may narrow the row with `select`.

ticketNumber.description:
The allocation's ticket number, as Sage shows it. Free text, not generated.
**Required**: Sage stores no allocation without one, so a request without it
is refused with `FIELD_REQUIRED`. (Optional in the schema only because the
field was added after the endpoint was published.)

orderNumber.description:
The allocation's order number, as Sage shows it under "Order #". Free text, at most 20
characters; longer is refused with `FIELD_INVALID`. Absent leaves it empty.

jobNumber.description:
Required when `purpose` is `JOB_REQUISITION`, and at status 4 whenever a line is on a
work-in-progress or direct-expense account, which Sage costs to a job.

status.description:
Absent means `1` (Open), which moves nothing. See `InventoryAllocationStatus`
for what each value moves.

description.description:
Free text, and **free text only**.

It has no effect on posting. Whether a job cost is written is decided by
`purpose`. **Required and not blank**: Sage stores no allocation without a
description, so a request without one is refused with `FIELD_REQUIRED`.

purpose.description: What the allocation is for. Replaces the magic string.

period.description:
Optional posting period, as on ledger transactions: derived from
`transactionDate` when absent, validated against `validPeriods` when present.

id.description: The row UUID. The only per-line unique value here.

recordNumber.description:
The Sage record number: **the allocation's, not the line's**. See the model
doc.

idRef.description:
The parent allocation's `id`, the value the child fetch joins on. Redundant
when read nested under the parent, which is the only way it can be read, but
it is in the child `SELECT` and therefore on the wire.

lineNumber.description: The line's position. The value that actually orders and distinguishes lines.

partRecordNumber.description:
The part's Sage record number, matching `Part.recordNumber`.

**The v3 write result for this same resource already publishes it under this
name** (`InventoryAllocationLineResult.partRecordNumber`), so the read model
matching it is what stops one resource spelling one value two ways.

partDescription.description: The part description. Copied from the part master when the caller omits it.

alphaNumber.description:
The alphanumeric part code a human reads.

Note that the `Part` entity publishes this same value under the name
`partCode`.

unitDescription.description: The unit of measure as text.

inventoryQuantity.description: The quantity moved. The write contract calls this `quantity`.

inventoryCost.description: The unit cost. The write contract calls this `cost`.

inventoryTotal.description:
`inventoryQuantity * inventoryCost`. The write contract calls this `total`,
and cross-checks it against the other two on the way in, returning 422 naming
both figures on a mismatch.

serialNumber.description:
The serial number of the item moved.

Nothing this API writes populates it, so a non-empty value here came from
Sage.

sourceLocation.description: The location stock is drawn from, matching the inventory-location lookup's record number.

debitAccount.description: The GL account the line debits.

debitSubAccount.description:
The sub-account under `debitAccount`. Spelled to match
`InventoryAllocationLineInput.debitSubAccount` on the write side of this same
resource.

destinationLocation.description:
The location stock is moved to. Present only on a transfer between locations,
in which case the line writes two history rows and two quantity movements:
one negative at `sourceLocation`, one positive here.

noteText.description: Free-text notes on the line. Line breaks are `\n`; the important note, the part Sage pops up when the record opens, is in `importantNote`. A filter on `noteText` matches the whole note, the important note included, and refuses a `|`.

importantNote.description:
The note's important part: the text Sage shows in a pop-up ("Important Note!") when the
record is opened. Line breaks are `\n`; empty when the note has none. Read only, and not
usable in a filter, a sort or a match: filter on `noteText`, which matches the whole note.
It is only ever added to (`POST /api/v3/notes`), never replaced or cleared.

InventoryAllocationLine.description:
One line of an inventory allocation, as read.

**`recordNumber` is the parent's, repeated on every line.** It carries the
allocation header's record number rather than a per-line sequence, so it is not
a line identifier and will not distinguish two lines of the same allocation;
`id` and `lineNumber` will.

**Three amounts on this model have a second set of names one hop away.**
`inventoryQuantity`, `inventoryCost` and `inventoryTotal` are what the read
surface calls them; the write contract calls the same three `quantity`, `cost`
and `total`, in both `InventoryAllocationLineInput` and
`InventoryAllocationLineResult`.

partNumber.description:
The part's Sage record number.

Note the name: on the read side the same value is published as
`partRecordNumber`; this write input spells it `partNumber`.

At status 3 or 4 the part must be a stock item and not serialized, as Sage requires a serial
number this endpoint cannot carry: otherwise the allocation is refused with `FIELD_INVALID`
(an unknown part with `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`), and nothing is written.

partDescription.description: Free text. Looked up from the part master when omitted.

quantity.description:
Must be greater than zero.

**No more than is available** at `sourceLocation` when the allocation moves
stock (status `3` or `4`): lines taking the same part out of the same
location are added together and compared with that location's available
quantity. An allocation that asks for more is refused with
`INSUFFICIENT_INVENTORY`, naming each part and location, and nothing is
written.

cost.description:
The unit cost.

**Required on a return** (a line with only `destinationLocation`): the stock comes back into
inventory at this cost. **Ignored on an issue or a transfer**, which the server values itself
at the part's average cost (or, for a company on FIFO or LIFO, from its cost layers); the
reply's line carries the cost and total used. At most six decimal places.

total.description:
`quantity * cost`, to the cent. Optional: when sent with `cost` it is **cross-checked by the
server**, which refuses the line naming both figures when they differ once each is rounded to
the cent (8 × 14.313224 is sent as 114.51). Absent, it is computed. Ignored on an issue or a
transfer, as `cost` is.

sourceLocation.description:
The location the stock leaves. With no `destinationLocation` the line is an
**issue**; with one it is a **transfer**. Omit it, and send only
`destinationLocation`, for a **return**: stock coming back into a location.
A line needs at least one of the two, or it is refused with `FIELD_REQUIRED`.

destinationLocation.description:
The location the stock arrives at. With `sourceLocation` the line is a
**transfer**; on its own it is a **return**.

debitAccount.description:
The account the line's cost is booked to: debited by an issue's journal,
credited by a return's. **Required on an issue or a return line**, refused
with `FIELD_REQUIRED` when missing. On a transfer it is ignored and nothing
is written: no cost moves between locations.

At status 4, a line on a work-in-progress or direct-expense account needs the allocation's
`jobNumber` (`FIELD_REQUIRED` without one), and a line on an equipment expense account is
refused with `EQUIPMENT_COST_INVALID`: an allocation to equipment is not built. Nothing is
written.

debitSubAccount.description: The sub-account under `debitAccount`. Ignored on a transfer, as `debitAccount` is.

costCode.description:
The job cost code this line's cost is booked under. **Required on every line
of a `JOB_REQUISITION` at status 4**, which books job cost; ignored
otherwise. Nothing is defaulted. Lines that share a cost code and cost type
are booked as one job cost. Install-specific: query the cost-code lookup
rather than hardcoding.

costType.description:
The job cost type for this line's cost, required and ignored exactly as
`costCode` is. Install-specific above 5: query the cost-type lookup rather
than hardcoding.

Where the company requires a cost type on expense accounts, a line that books job cost must
be coded with its account's own cost type, and its account must have one; otherwise the
allocation is refused with `FIELD_INVALID` and nothing is written.

recordNumber.description:
**The parent document's record number, repeated on every line.** Sage keys
lines on their parent's record number, so this is not a per-line identity: use
`id`, or `recordNumber` together with `lineNumber`.

sourceLocation.description: The location the stock left; `0` on a return, which names only `destinationLocation`.

InventoryAllocationStatus.description:
An inventory allocation's status.

Status decides what moves. `1` and `2` record the allocation and its lines and
move no stock at all; `3` reduces the available quantity at each line's source
location and nothing else; `4` ships: it reduces available quantity, the
location's on-hand quantity and the part master's on-hand total (or, for a return,
raises them), posts to the general ledger and books job cost. Inventory history is
written for `4` only.

The meanings below are the ones Sage uses. They are **not** draft, approved,
delivered and invoiced, whatever else you may have been told.
x-enum-descriptions: Open. Inventory is available. Moves nothing.
Review. Review before shipping. Moves nothing.
Hold Stock. Reserved for a job or work order. Reduces available quantity at the source location only; no history, job cost or journal.
Shipped. Sent to a job. Reduces available and both on-hand columns, posts the journal and books job cost.

document.description: The document itself, with its lines.

ledgerTransaction.description: Absent when the document did not post to the general ledger.

jobCosts.description: Always present, empty when none were written.

inventory.description: Always present, empty when nothing moved.

dryRun.description:
`true` when this response describes a rolled-back write rather than a
committed one. See `dryRun` on the request.

Always present, so a body is self-describing on its own: a stored response, a
log line or a support ticket says which kind of write it was without needing
the request beside it. Declared here rather than on `WriteResult` so the
service-inventory envelope, which substitutes its own, cannot be the one that
forgets to say.

period.description: The period the server resolved and posted into.

year.description: The fiscal year the server resolved and posted into.

InventoryAllocationWriteResult.description:
The body of a successful `POST /inventory-allocations`.

`jobCosts` holds one job cost for each distinct cost code and cost type on a
`JOB_REQUISITION` at status 3 or 4, and is empty for any other allocation.

recordNumber.description:
The Sage record number.

**This is the value the other inventory entities store as their location
code**, and there is a width disagreement worth knowing about before writing
a join: the location number is a 64-bit integer here, while every field that
points at it is published as a 32-bit integer. A location number above the
32-bit range would be unrepresentable on the referring side; no install is
near that, but the asymmetry is real and is not a modelling choice made here.

locationName.description: The location's name. The only human-facing value on the record.

employeeNumber.description:
The employee responsible for the location, as an `Employee` record number.
`0` when unset, which is why it is `int64` rather than `RecordNumber`
(`@minValue(1)`), matching `Client.employeeNumber`.

InventoryLocation.description:
The inventory-location master.

Four columns and that is the whole record. It is the lookup behind every
location code the inventory entities carry: `locationNumber` on
`InventoryQuantity`, `InventoryHistory` and `InventorySerial`, and
`sourceLocation` / `destinationLocation` on `InventoryAllocationLine`, all
resolve here. There is no second location lookup in the schema.

**This API never writes an inventory location.** Locations are created in Sage;
the entity is read-only.

**Only `id` and `recordNumber` are required.** Every other field is optional
because a query may narrow the row with `select`.

historyRecordNumber.description: Present when an inventory-history row was written.

idRef.description:
The part row's UUID.

Unlike `idRef` on a line model, this one is **not** a child-collection
pointer: this is a top-level entity and there is no request that returns it
nested under its part. The value is in the projection and therefore on the
wire, and it is the only join back to the part that does not go through a
record number.

partRecordNumber.description:
The part's record number.

This is the part's record number, not the human-readable part code. That is
`Part.partCode`.

quantityOnHand.description:
The physically-present quantity.

**On-hand and available move on different events.** A `3-Hold Stock`
allocation reduces `quantityAvailable` only (the stock is reserved but still
in the bin), while `4-Shipped` reduces both (see
`InventoryAllocationStatus`). Reading only this field understates what is
spoken for.

quantityAvailable.description: The unreserved quantity. Moves for both `3-Hold Stock` and `4-Shipped`.

lastCountDate.description: The last physical count. Date, not an instant.

beginningQuantity.description: The period-opening quantity. The write path seeds it to `0` on a new row.

minRestockLevel.description: The reorder point, a whole quantity.

maxRestockLevel.description: The restock-to level, a whole quantity.

InventoryQuantity.description:
One part's stock position at one location.

**This entity has no `recordNumber`, and that is how Sage stores it, not an
omission.** These rows carry no Sage record number at all, so the convention
that `id` and `recordNumber` are the two guaranteed fields cannot hold here.
`id` is the only required field on this model. The row's natural key is the pair
(part, location).

The absence has a second, non-obvious consequence. Paging is made deterministic
by ordering on the record number and then on the row UUID; with no record number
this entity is ordered on the UUID alone. Paging is still stable, but the order
is UUID order, which is not part number order and not insertion order.

**Only `id` is required.** Every other field is optional because a query may
narrow the row with `select`.

recordNumber.description:
The Sage record number: the job number a human reads in Sage.

On a new job you may choose it; leave it out and Sage's next number is
used.

shortName.description: The abbreviated name Sage shows in pick lists.

clientNumber.description: The client this job bills to; the `Client` entity's `recordNumber`.

contact.description:
A person's name, free text. Not a foreign key.

Read only: Sage keeps a job's contacts in its contact list now, and
clears this older field when its own interface saves a job.

phoneNumber.description: Free text as Sage stores it; no format is imposed. Read only, as `contact`.

architect.description: The architect: a vendor's `recordNumber`. Absent or `0` when unset.

lender.description: The lender: a vendor's `recordNumber`. Absent or `0` when unset.

supervisor.description: The supervising employee's record number. `0` when unset.

salesperson.description:
The selling employee's record number. `0` when unset.

A job carries dedicated salesperson, estimator and supervisor references, so
each keeps its role name here rather than sharing the general
`employeeNumber` spelling used on `Client`.

estimator.description: The estimating employee's record number. `0` when unset.

userDefined1.description: Free text, meaning defined per install.

userDefined2.description: Free text, meaning defined per install.

payrollLocale.description:
A record number into the payroll local-tax (locale) table. Install-specific; not an enum.

Read only.

salesTaxDistrict.description: The job's sales tax district: a tax district's `recordNumber`.

ledgerAccount.description:
The job's income account.

**Published as `ledgerAccount`**, the spelling used for a ledger account
everywhere else in this API.

Sage refuses an account that the ledger setup uses as one of its default
control accounts (receivables, service receivables, payables, inventory,
equipment, accumulated depreciation, and loans): such a write is refused
with `FIELD_INVALID` on this field.

department.description: A record number into the department table. `0` when unset.

discountTerms.description:
A **terms string** on a job, not a date.

The same underlying field carries a date on the invoice entities, where it is
published as `discountDate`. Do not assume `YYYY-MM-DD` here.

dueTerms.description: A terms string on a job, not a date. See `discountTerms`.

discountRate.description: The discount rate. JSON string at native scale; a generated client must type it as a string, not a number.

retainageRate.description: Retainage rate held back from billings.

beginningBalance.description: The job's beginning balance. Moved only by posting; no write sets it.

endingBalance.description: The job's ending balance. Moved only by posting; no write sets it.

bidDate.description: The bid date. A date, not an instant: no time component is returned.

contractDate.description: The contract date. A date, not an instant.

startDate.description: The start date. A date, not an instant.

completionDate.description: The completion date. A date, not an instant.

jobType.description:
The job type. Install-specific, so the codes are not enumerated in this
contract; query the job-type lookup rather than hardcoding values.

status.description: The job's status. Job status does not restrict posting. See `JobStatus`.

postToWip.description:
A `0`/`1` flag, not a boolean on the wire: whether the job posts to work in progress.

Setting it to `1`, on a new job or on a job that had `0`, adds the job as a
subaccount of every ledger account set up for job subaccounts, as Sage
offers to when you tick the box (it pre-selects them all). A subaccount the
job already has is left as it is.

certifiedPayroll.description: A `0`/`1` flag: whether the job requires certified payroll reporting.

contractNumber.description:
**Free text, not a record number**, despite the `Number` suffix: the contract
identifier as the customer writes it.

clientPO.description: **Free text**: the client's own purchase-order number for this job. Not a reference to a purchase order in this API.

noteText.description: A free-text memo attached to the job. Line breaks are `\n`; the important note, the part Sage pops up when the record opens, is in `importantNote`. A filter on `noteText` matches the whole note, the important note included, and refuses a `|`. On a write: a create stores the note as sent; a change adds it on a new line after the stored note (`noteMode` `append`, the default) or replaces it (`noteMode` `replace`), and `null` clears it. A write never changes the important note. A `|`, U+001E or another control character is refused with `FIELD_INVALID`.

importantNote.description:
The note's important part: the text Sage shows in a pop-up ("Important Note!") when the
record is opened. Line breaks are `\n`; empty when the note has none. Read only, and not
usable in a filter, a sort or a match: filter on `noteText`, which matches the whole note.
It is only ever added to (`POST /api/v3/notes`), never replaced or cleared.

isInactive.description: A `0`/`1` flag despite the `is` prefix; Sage stores an integer and v3 does not reshape it.

phases.description:
Child collection `phases`, the job's phases, requested via `children: ["phases"]`.

On a write, a phase is named by its `phaseNumber`: a number the job has
changes that phase (only the fields you send), and a new number adds a
phase, which needs a `phaseName`. A phase you leave out is kept; a phase
cannot be renumbered or removed through this API. Every job has phase `0`,
"None", from the moment it is created: you may rename it or set its other
fields, here or on a new job, but never add it. Sending the same phase
number twice is refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

Job.description:
The job (3-5 Jobs).

**This is the job header, not the job cost.** Job costs are a separate entity.

Its one child collection is `phases`, requested with `children: ["phases"]`. A
job carries no last-changed stamp, so `lastUpdated` filtering is not supported
here.

**Only `id` and `recordNumber` are guaranteed.** A query may narrow the row
with `select`, so every other field is absent unless it was asked for.

id.description: The row UUID. The only unique key on this entity; see the model note.

recordNumber.description:
**The job number**: the `Job` entity's `recordNumber`, not a per-row record
number. Not unique. See the model note.

phaseNumber.description:
Sage's "Phase#". The identifier every phase reference targets.

On a job write it names the phase: a whole number, `0` or more, that
cannot be changed once the phase exists.

phaseName.description:
The phase's name, which Sage labels "Description". Published as `phaseName`.

Required when a job write adds a phase.

retention.description:
A retention **rate**, not an amount.

The same underlying value is published as `retainageRate` on a job and
`primaryRate` on a progress billing: three names for one concept.

unitDescription.description:
Sage's "Unit": the unit of measure the phase's quantity is counted in.

Spelled `unitDescription` here and `unitDesc` on a cost code: one concept,
two published names, both carried forward.

noteText.description: A free-text memo on the phase. Line breaks are `\n`; the important note, the part Sage pops up when the record opens, is in `importantNote`. A filter on `noteText` matches the whole note, the important note included, and refuses a `|`. On a write: a new line stores the note as sent; a changed line's note is added on a new line after the stored note, or replaces it, per the job change's `noteMode`, and `null` clears it. A write never changes the important note. A `|`, U+001E or another control character is refused with `FIELD_INVALID`.

importantNote.description:
The note's important part: the text Sage shows in a pop-up ("Important Note!") when the
record is opened. Line breaks are `\n`; empty when the note has none. Read only, and not
usable in a filter, a sort or a match: filter on `noteText`, which matches the whole note.
It is only ever added to (`POST /api/v3/notes`), never replaced or cleared.

JobPhase.description:
A job phase (3-5 Jobs, the Phases tab).

**`recordNumber` on a phase is the JOB number, not this row's identity.** Sage
labels it "Job#". So `recordNumber` here is not unique (every phase of one job
carries the same value), and `id` is the only key that identifies a row.
`phaseNumber` is what distinguishes phases within a job, and it is what every
phase reference in the product points at (`Subcontract.phaseNumber`,
`JobCost.phaseNumber`), **not** `recordNumber`.

The job projection line entities (budget, cost-to-complete, hours-to-complete,
units-complete) share this shape, carrying the job's number rather than their
own; a job cost does not — its record number really is its own.

A job carries its phases too, as `Job.phases` (`children: ["phases"]`), and a
phase is written only there, with its job: this entity is read only.

Sage records a "Model" against a phase, which this API does not return.

JobStatus.description:
The job's own status.

Six members, and note it does **not** share the `1-Open` / `2-Review` /
`3-Dispute` opening that several other Sage status families have. A caller that
learned `3` means Dispute from a job cost and applied that reading to a job
would read a live contract as a disputed one. Status codes are per record type;
never carry a meaning across from one to another.

recordNumber.description:
The general ledger account number itself.

Typed `RecordNumber` rather than `LedgerAccountNumber` because it is this
entity's own record number; the `LedgerAccountNumber` scalar marks the
*references* that point back here.

shortName.description: The abbreviated name Sage shows in pick lists.

subsidiaryType.description:
Sage's "Subsidiary Type": whether the account is subsidiary-tracked.

**Not a subaccount number**, despite what the name suggests in Sage. The
underlying value carries four different meanings across the product
(`subAccount`, `subaccount`, `subaccountNumber` and this one), and on the
chart of accounts it is a type code. Install-specific; not an enum.

summaryAccount.description: The account this one rolls up into, itself a `recordNumber` on this entity. Null when it does not roll up.

costType.description:
The cost type, matching the `CostType` entity's `recordNumber`.

`1`-`5` are Sage presets and **`6`-`9` are per-company**, so this is
deliberately not an enum. Query the cost-type lookup (`CostType`).

beginningBalance.description: The balance the account carried into the current year.

endBalance.description: Sage's "Ending Balance". Published as `endingBalance` on `Job`; see the model note.

lastCheck.description:
Sage's "LastCheck": the last cheque number written on the account.

Meaningful only on a cash account.

lastDeposit.description: Sage's "LastDeposit": the last deposit recorded on the account.

startingBalance.description: The balance the account was opened at. Distinct from `beginningBalance`.

accountType.description:
The account's category.

**Deliberately not an enum**: the category an account number actually falls
into is decided by the seventeen account-number ranges on `LedgerSetup`,
which are configured per installation. Resolve against those rather than
assuming a fixed set here.

debitCredit.description:
Which side the account normally carries: `1` is debit-normal, `2` is

returned.

RequestState.description:
Where a request stands.

- `pending`: sent to the on-premise agent, and it can still start.
- `unconfirmed`: its start-by has passed and the agent has not answered. It was very probably never
started, but that is not confirmed until the agent reports. A running agent reports within a few
minutes that it never started the request (`expired`, `503 REQUEST_EXPIRED`: nothing was written).
A request the agent started and never answered, or whose agent is not heard from, resolves an hour
after its start-by to `500 OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, which an operator confirms in Sage before any retry.
- `cancel_requested`: a cancel was accepted before the request started; its outcome follows.
- `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `expired`: the request's outcome.

requestId.description: The request id, as returned in `OPDC-Request-Id`.

startBy.description:
The moment after which the on-premise agent will not start the request. A write not started by
then is refused, and nothing is written.

execBudget.description: How long the request may run once started, for example `20s`.

finishedAt.description: When the request's outcome was recorded.

statusCode.description: The HTTP status the request answered with, once it has an outcome.

errorCode.description: The error code it answered with, when its outcome was a failure.

cancelRequestedAt.description: When a cancel for it was accepted.

hostLastSeenAt.description:
While the request has no outcome: when the company's on-premise agent was last heard from. Absent
when it has not been heard from at all.

RequestStatus.description:
A request that has not answered yet, or the summary of one whose response is no longer held.

**A `202` carrying this body is not success.** Nothing may have been written yet. Follow `Location`
(or poll `GET /api/v3/requests/{requestId}`) until it answers something other than `202`.

recordNumber.description:
The part this price is for: the `Part` entity's `recordNumber`.

Not this row's own number. See the model doc.

lineNumber.description:
The row's position within the part's list. Two digits, so Sage caps the list short.

When changing a part's `vendorPrices`, a line with a `lineNumber` changes that stored line and
a line without one is added; a stored line you leave out is kept. On a new part the lines are
numbered in the order sent.

preferenceNum.description:
Sage's "Preference#": where this vendor ranks for this part, `1` being first
choice.

Not a foreign key and not a record number, despite the `Num` in the name.

vendorNumber.description: The vendor quoting this price: the `Vendor` entity's `recordNumber`.

vendorOrder.description:
Sage's "Order#": the vendor's own catalogue number for this part, free text.

Not an order and not a reference to a purchase order. It is what goes on a
purchase order so the vendor recognises the item.

discountRate.description: Sage's "Disc. Rate". A rate, not an amount.

vendorPrice.description:
The vendor's unit price for the part. JSON string, native scale.

**Six decimal places, and the string encoding is what preserves them.** This
is the same scale as the unit price on an invoice line. A client that parses
the value into a two-decimal type will round a unit price such as `0.003125`
to `0.00`.

lastUpdated.description:
The stored last-updated date. A date, not an instant.

**This is not the value a `lastUpdated` filter compares against.** It is
defaulted when the row is created and is not maintained on edit, and it is
absent altogether on some company databases, so it may be older than the
record's real last change. The filter uses Sage's maintained update stamp
instead. Drive an incremental sync from your own previous run time rather than
from this value.

VendorPartPrice.description:
Sage's "Vendor Part Prices", as read.

What each vendor charges for a part, ranked by preference. Sage files it under
menu **9-2, Parts**, not under 4-4, Vendors, and that is the correct way to read
it: it is a part's list of vendors, not a vendor's list of parts.

**`recordNumber` here is the *part's* record number.** Sage keys these rows on
the part they price, numbering them within the part by `lineNumber`. So a filter
on `recordNumber` returns every vendor's price for one part, which is not what
the name suggests. The name follows the rule every line collection in the
product uses (a line publishes its parent's record number as `recordNumber`), so
it is accurate about the family and misleading about this row.

This is the one place the two spellings meet in one model: `recordNumber` is the
part and `vendorNumber` is the vendor, on the same row.

Every field but `id` and `recordNumber` is optional because a request may narrow
the response with `select`.
